record.field: These transactions involve the sale of goods or services to customers, either on credit (accounts receivable) or for immediate payment (cash sales). Sales transactions increase revenue and are recorded based on the accrual accounting principle (when earned).

These transactions involve collecting cash from customers, either in the form of payments for current sales (cash sales) or collections of accounts receivable (credit sales). Cash receipts are recorded when the payment is received, regardless of when the sale occurred.

These transactions occur when customers return goods after a sale or receive allowances (price reductions) due to defective or damaged goods. These reduce the company’s total sales and result in adjustments to accounts receivable or cash refunds.

Bad debts occur when a company determines that an outstanding receivable is unlikely to be collected. The company may write off these receivables as uncollectible, reducing accounts receivable and recognizing a bad debt expense.

This is an estimate of the portion of accounts receivable that the company expects to be uncollectible. It is recorded as an expense in the same period as the related sales to adhere to the matching principle.

These transactions involve acquiring inventory, supplies, or services from suppliers. Purchases can be made on credit (accounts payable) or for immediate payment (cash purchases). This is the starting point of the acquisition cycle, and it impacts inventory (for goods) or expenses (for services) and liabilities (accounts payable).

These transactions represent payments made to suppliers for goods or services that were previously acquired, either on credit or for immediate payment. They reduce the company’s cash balance and accounts payable.

Purchase returns occur when a company returns goods to a supplier due to defects or other reasons. Purchase allowances are reductions in the amount owed to a supplier due to damaged goods or poor service, without returning the goods. Both types of transactions reduce the amount owed (accounts payable) and may affect inventory or expense accounts.

These transactions involve acquiring raw materials, finished goods, or other inventory items from suppliers. These purchases can be made on credit (resulting in accounts payable) or with immediate cash payments.

When goods are received from a supplier, the receiving department typically checks the items against the purchase order (PO) and records them as inventory. The receipt of inventory is an internal control point that ensures only authorized purchases are accepted.

Inventory may be transferred between different locations within a company, such as between warehouses or production departments. These movements should be tracked to maintain accurate records of inventory quantities at each location.

These transactions involve adjusting inventory records for discrepancies between physical stock counts and the amounts recorded in the system. Shrinkage can occur due to theft, damage, spoilage, or errors. Obsolete inventory is written down when it is no longer usable or sellable.

COGS represents the direct costs of producing goods that have been sold. When inventory is sold, the cost associated with that inventory is transferred from the balance sheet to the income statement as COGS. This is a key element in determining a company’s gross profit.
Inventory Returns (Sales Returns and Purchase Returns)

Sales Returns: These transactions occur when customers return goods after a sale. The returned goods are added back to inventory, and the cost of those goods is subtracted from COGS. Purchase Returns: When the company returns goods to a supplier, inventory is reduced, and accounts payable is adjusted if the original purchase was made on credit.
These transactions involve repaying the principal and interest on borrowed funds. The principal repayment reduces the company's liabilities, and interest payments are recorded as an expense.
Purchase of Property, Plan, and Equipment (Acquisition /addition)
These transactions involve purchasing or internally constructing assets such as land, buildings, machinery, or equipment. Acquisitions increase the PPE balance on the balance sheet.

These transactions involve raising capital through borrowing from lenders, such as banks or issuing bonds to the public. The company receives cash in exchange for agreeing to repay the borrowed amount with interest over time. Debt issuance increases the company’s liabilities and cash.
These transactions involve raising capital by issuing shares of stock to investors. The company receives cash in exchange for ownership shares, increasing both cash and shareholders’ equity.

When a company buys back its own shares from the market, it reduces shareholders’ equity. Treasury stock represents shares that are issued but not outstanding and can be reissued later or retired permanently.

These transactions involve distributing a portion of the company’s earnings to shareholders. Dividends can be paid in cash or stock and represent a return on investment to shareholders. Dividends reduce retained earnings and cash (for cash dividends).

Companies use either a periodic or perpetual inventory system to track inventory. Periodic System: Inventory is only updated at the end of a period when a physical count is performed. Purchases are recorded in a purchases account, and inventory adjustments are made at the end of the period. Perpetual System: Inventory is updated continuously in real-time whenever transactions like purchases, sales, and returns occur.

The method used to value inventory affects both the cost of inventory and COGS. Common valuation methods include: • FIFO (First-In, First-Out): The oldest inventory is sold first. • LIFO (Last-In, First-Out): The most recently acquired inventory is sold first. • Weighted Average: The cost of goods sold and ending inventory are based on the average cost of all units available for sale.
Manufacturing Transactions (Work in Process, Finished Goods)

For manufacturing companies, inventory is divided into raw materials, work-in-process (WIP), and finished goods. When raw materials are used in production, their cost is transferred to WIP, and once production is complete, the cost is transferred to finished goods.
Sales of Property, Plan, and Equipment (Disposals)

These transactions occur when an asset is sold, scrapped, or otherwise removed from service. Disposals decrease the PPE balance and may result in a gain or loss on disposal, which affects the income statement.
Depreciation of Property, Plant, and Equipment
Depreciation is the periodic allocation of the cost of an asset over its useful life. It reduces the asset’s book value on the balance sheet and is recognized as an expense on the income statement.
Impairment of Property, Plant, and Equipment

Impairment occurs when the carrying value of an asset exceeds its recoverable amount (the higher of fair value less costs to sell or its value in use). This results in a write-down of the asset's value on the balance sheet.
Regular expenses incurred to maintain or restore an asset’s productive capacity. These do not increase the useful life or enhance the asset’s capacity and are expensed in the period incurred.

These are expenditures that extend the useful life of an asset, enhance its capacity, or improve its efficiency. Unlike repairs, these expenditures are capitalized and increase the book value of the PPE.
These transactions occur when the business buys investments, such as stocks, bonds, real estate, or other financial instruments. They increase the company’s investments on the balance sheet.

These transactions occur when the company sells or disposes of investments. Disposals reduce the investments on the balance sheet and may result in a gain or loss on the sale, affecting the income statement.

These transactions represent earnings from investments, such as dividends from equity securities or interest from bonds. This income affects the income statement and is usually recognized when earned.
Realized Gains or Losses on Investments

Realized gains or losses are recognized when an investment is sold, and the difference between the sale price and the book value is recorded. These gains or losses directly affect the income statement.

Impairment occurs when there is a permanent decline in the value of an investment, such as the bankruptcy of a company whose shares are held. Impairments result in a write-down of the investment’s value and affect the income statement.
Investment in Subsidiaries or Joint Ventures

These transactions involve making equity investments in subsidiaries or joint ventures, where the business takes a significant or controlling interest in another entity. The accounting treatment varies based on the level of control or influence.

Sales discounts are reductions offered to customers as incentives for early payment. These discounts are typically offered under terms such as "2/10, net 30," meaning a 2% discount is given if payment is made within 10 days, otherwise the full amount is due in 30 days. Sales discounts reduce the total receivable amount and are recorded separately as a contra-revenue account.
In some cases, customers may make payments in advance of receiving goods or services. These receipts are recorded as a liability (unearned revenue) until the company delivers the goods or services.
For some sales, companies charge customers separately for shipping or freight costs. These charges are added to the total sales amount and recorded as revenue.

Purchase discounts (also called cash discounts) are reductions in the amount payable to suppliers if payments are made within a certain time period (e.g., "2/10, net 30" means a 2% discount if paid within 10 days). These discounts incentivize early payments and reduce the total payment made to suppliers.

These transactions involve costs incurred by the company for shipping goods from suppliers to their location. Freight charges are typically added to the cost of inventory or expenses. In some cases, the company may need to record freight separately.

At the end of an accounting period, companies may receive goods or services that haven’t yet been billed by the supplier. To reflect the obligation to pay in the correct period, the company accrues a liability for the unbilled purchases.

These transactions occur when a company pays a supplier in advance for goods or services to be received in the future. Prepayments are initially recorded as assets (prepaid expenses) and are expensed over time as the goods or services are received.

Certain acquisitions are directly recorded as expenses, particularly when goods or services are immediately consumed or when services are rendered. These expenses affect the income statement in the period in which they are incurred.
Unrealized Gains or Losses on Investments

Unrealized gains or losses arise from changes in the fair market value of investments that are still held by the company. These are recorded when the company marks its investments to market, typically at period-end. They affect the balance sheet and, depending on the accounting treatment (held for trading or available-for-sale securities), may also affect the income statement or other comprehensive income.

Stock dividends involve issuing additional shares to existing shareholders instead of cash. Stock splits increase the number of shares outstanding by dividing each share into multiple shares without changing the total equity.

Certain debt agreements contain covenants requiring the company to maintain specific financial ratios or make certain financial disclosures. Any costs associated with complying with loan covenants, such as legal fees, are recorded as expenses.

Convertible bonds or preferred stock can be converted into common stock at the option of the holder. These transactions involve complex accounting because they combine features of both debt and equity.

These transactions involve paying interest on borrowed funds. Interest payments are considered expenses and reduce the company's cash balance. These payments may occur periodically (e.g., monthly, quarterly, or annually) depending on the terms of the debt agreement.

Transaksi ini melibatkan penjualan barang atau jasa kepada pelanggan, baik secara kredit (piutang usaha) maupun pembayaran langsung (penjualan tunai). Transaksi penjualan meningkatkan pendapatan dan dicatat berdasarkan prinsip akrual (saat diperoleh).

Transaksi ini berupa penerimaan kas dari pelanggan, baik atas penjualan saat ini (penjualan tunai) maupun penagihan piutang usaha (penjualan kredit). Penerimaan kas dicatat saat kas diterima terlepas dari kapan penjualan terjadi.

Transaksi ini terjadi saat pelanggan mengembalikan barang setelah penjualan atau menerima pengurangan harga karena barang cacat/rusak. Ini menurunkan total penjualan dan menghasilkan penyesuaian piutang usaha atau pengembalian kas.

Piutang tak tertagih terjadi ketika perusahaan menetapkan suatu piutang tidak mungkin ditagih. Piutang tersebut dihapus (write-off), menurunkan piutang usaha dan diakui sebagai beban piutang tak tertagih.
Ini adalah estimasi bagian piutang usaha yang diperkirakan tidak tertagih. Dicatat sebagai beban pada periode yang sama dengan penjualan terkait untuk menerapkan prinsip matching.

Transaksi ini melibatkan perolehan persediaan, perlengkapan, atau jasa dari pemasok. Pembelian dapat secara kredit (utang usaha) atau tunai. Ini adalah titik awal siklus akuisisi dan memengaruhi persediaan (barang) atau beban (jasa) serta utang usaha.
Transaksi berupa pembayaran kepada pemasok atas barang atau jasa yang sebelumnya diperoleh, baik kredit maupun tunai. Mengurangi saldo kas dan utang usaha.

Retur terjadi saat perusahaan mengembalikan barang ke pemasok karena cacat atau alasan lain. Pengurangan harga adalah penurunan jumlah terutang tanpa pengembalian barang. Keduanya menurunkan utang usaha dan dapat memengaruhi persediaan atau beban.
Transaksi ini melibatkan pembelian bahan baku, barang jadi, atau item persediaan lain dari pemasok, baik secara kredit (utang usaha) maupun tunai.

Saat barang diterima dari pemasok, bagian penerimaan memeriksa terhadap Purchase Order dan mencatatnya sebagai persediaan. Penerimaan adalah titik pengendalian internal untuk memastikan hanya pembelian yang sah diterima.
Persediaan dapat dipindahkan antar lokasi seperti gudang atau departemen produksi. Pergerakan harus dilacak untuk menjaga akurasi kuantitas per lokasi.

Transaksi ini menyesuaikan catatan persediaan atas selisih antara jumlah fisik dan sistem. Kehilangan bisa karena pencurian, kerusakan, kadaluarsa, atau kesalahan. Persediaan usang diturunkan nilainya ketika tidak lagi dapat digunakan atau dijual.
HPP merepresentasikan biaya langsung produksi barang yang dijual. Saat persediaan terjual, biaya terkait dipindahkan dari neraca ke laba rugi sebagai HPP. Ini elemen kunci penentuan laba kotor.

Retur Penjualan: terjadi saat pelanggan mengembalikan barang; barang kembali ke persediaan dan HPP disesuaikan. Retur Pembelian: saat perusahaan mengembalikan barang ke pemasok, persediaan turun dan utang disesuaikan.
Transaksi ini melibatkan pembayaran kembali pokok dan bunga atas dana yang dipinjam. Pokok menurunkan liabilitas dan bunga dicatat sebagai beban.
Transaksi ini mencakup pembelian atau konstruksi internal aset seperti tanah, bangunan, mesin, atau peralatan. Perolehan meningkatkan saldo aset tetap (PPE).
Transaksi ini menggalang modal melalui pinjaman dari bank atau penerbitan obligasi. Perusahaan menerima kas dan berkomitmen mengembalikan pokok plus bunga. Meningkatkan liabilitas dan kas.
Transaksi ini menggalang modal dengan menerbitkan saham kepada investor. Perusahaan menerima kas dan meningkatkan kas serta ekuitas pemegang saham.
Saat perusahaan membeli kembali sahamnya di pasar, ekuitas pemegang saham berkurang. Saham treasury adalah saham yang diterbitkan namun tidak beredar dan dapat diterbitkan ulang atau dipensiunkan.
Transaksi ini mendistribusikan sebagian laba perusahaan kepada pemegang saham dalam bentuk kas atau saham. Dividen mengurangi laba ditahan dan kas (untuk dividen kas).

Perusahaan memakai sistem periodik atau perpetual. Sistem Periodik: Persediaan diperbarui di akhir periode setelah hitung fisik; pembelian dicatat di akun pembelian. Sistem Perpetual: Persediaan diperbarui terus menerus saat terjadi pembelian, penjualan, dan retur.
Metode penilaian memengaruhi biaya persediaan dan HPP. Metode umum: FIFO (masuk pertama keluar pertama), LIFO (masuk terakhir keluar pertama), Rata-rata Tertimbang.
Pada perusahaan manufaktur, persediaan dibagi bahan baku, barang dalam proses (BDP), dan barang jadi. Saat bahan baku dipakai, biayanya dipindah ke BDP, lalu ke barang jadi setelah selesai.
Terjadi saat aset dijual, dibuang, atau dihentikan pemakaiannya. Menurunkan saldo aset tetap dan dapat menghasilkan laba/rugi pelepasan.
Depresiasi adalah alokasi periodik biaya aset sepanjang umur manfaatnya. Mengurangi nilai buku di neraca dan diakui sebagai beban.
Penurunan nilai terjadi saat nilai tercatat aset melebihi jumlah terpulihkan. Menghasilkan penurunan nilai aset di neraca.
Beban rutin untuk mempertahankan atau memulihkan kapasitas produktif aset. Tidak menambah umur manfaat atau kapasitas; dibebankan pada periode terjadinya.
Pengeluaran yang memperpanjang umur manfaat, menambah kapasitas, atau meningkatkan efisiensi aset. Dikapitalisasi dan menaikkan nilai buku aset tetap.
Transaksi saat bisnis membeli investasi seperti saham, obligasi, real estat, atau instrumen keuangan lain. Meningkatkan akun investasi di neraca.
Transaksi saat perusahaan menjual atau melepas investasi. Menurunkan investasi dan dapat menimbulkan laba/rugi penjualan di laba rugi.
Pendapatan dari investasi seperti dividen atas sekuritas ekuitas atau bunga dari obligasi. Diakui di laba rugi saat diperoleh.
Diakui saat investasi dijual; selisih harga jual dan nilai buku dicatat. Mempengaruhi laba rugi.
Terjadi saat ada penurunan permanen nilai investasi (misal kebangkrutan pihak penerbit). Mengakibatkan penurunan nilai dan memengaruhi laba rugi.
Investasi pada Entitas Anak atau Ventura Bersama
Transaksi berupa investasi ekuitas di entitas anak atau ventura bersama dengan pengaruh signifikan atau kontrol. Perlakuan akuntansi bergantung tingkat pengaruh atau kontrol.
Diskon penjualan adalah pengurangan yang ditawarkan kepada pelanggan sebagai insentif pembayaran lebih awal (misal 2/10, net 30). Mengurangi jumlah piutang dan dicatat sebagai akun kontra pendapatan.
Pelanggan kadang membayar di muka sebelum barang/jasa diterima. Dicatat sebagai liabilitas (pendapatan ditangguhkan) sampai penyerahan dilakukan.
Untuk beberapa penjualan, perusahaan membebankan biaya pengiriman/angkut kepada pelanggan secara terpisah. Biaya ini ditambahkan ke total penjualan dan dicatat sebagai pendapatan.
Diskon pembelian (cash discount) adalah pengurangan jumlah terutang bila dibayar dalam periode tertentu (misal 2/10, net 30). Mendorong pembayaran lebih cepat dan menurunkan total pembayaran.
Transaksi ini adalah biaya pengiriman barang dari pemasok ke lokasi perusahaan. Biasanya ditambahkan ke biaya persediaan atau beban dan kadang dicatat terpisah.
Liabilitas Akrual atas Pembelian Belum Ditagih
Di akhir periode, perusahaan mungkin menerima barang/jasa yang belum ditagih. Untuk mencerminkan kewajiban dengan benar, perusahaan mengakui liabilitas akrual atas pembelian belum ditagih.
Transaksi saat perusahaan membayar pemasok di muka atas barang/jasa yang akan diterima. Dicatat sebagai aset (biaya dibayar dimuka) lalu diamortisasi saat diterima.
Beberapa akuisisi langsung dicatat sebagai beban saat barang/jasa segera dikonsumsi atau jasa telah diberikan. Mempengaruhi laba rugi pada periode terjadinya.
Muncul dari perubahan nilai wajar investasi yang masih dimiliki. Dicatat saat mark-to-market di akhir periode; memengaruhi neraca dan tergantung klasifikasi dapat memengaruhi laba rugi atau OCI.
Dividen saham menerbitkan saham tambahan kepada pemegang saham alih-alih kas. Stock split menambah jumlah saham beredar tanpa mengubah total ekuitas.
Perjanjian utang mengandung covenant mewajibkan pemeliharaan rasio keuangan atau pengungkapan tertentu. Biaya kepatuhan seperti biaya hukum dicatat sebagai beban.
Obligasi konversi atau saham preferen dapat dikonversi menjadi saham biasa oleh pemegang. Akuntansinya kompleks karena menggabungkan fitur utang dan ekuitas.
Transaksi ini berupa pembayaran bunga atas dana yang dipinjam. Bunga adalah beban dan mengurangi kas. Pembayaran dilakukan periodik sesuai syarat perjanjian utang.
